title: ANZ lifts year-end Brent forecast to $105 as tight physical market persists
body: A $105 year-end call implies little relief for crude-importing economies, with Asian importers including Japan, India and South Korea most exposed through their currencies and trade balances. The asymmetry is notable. The bank's upside risk sits about $15 above its base case, while its downside scenario needs both diplomatic and shipping breakthroughs, so the risk skew still favours higher prices. That supports energy equities and producer currencies such as the Canadian and Norwegian kroner exchange rates, and keeps upward pressure on headline inflation and bond yields across fuel-importing economies. Traders are likely to stay highly sensitive to headlines on Iran and on tanker traffic through Middle East shipping lanes. --- High oil prices will also keep the upside pressure on Australian inflation: RBA set for back-to-back hike after hot CPI, says Natixis' Garcia Herrero --- ANZ thinks oil stays expensive until the ships move freely again, and a peace deal on paper won't be enough on its own.

title: Binance pauses withdrawals after suspected $3B+ hack as Tether, Circle freeze $2.4B
body: The market has largely moved past the initial shock. BNB has bounced off its low and bitcoin is steady near $78,800, which suggests traders see the freezes and CZ's pledge as limiting the damage to Binance itself. The next risk is supply. The attacker holds more than $1 billion in ether and has already been selling smaller tokens on decentralised exchanges, so large ETH sales could weigh on ether's price. Partial withdrawal pauses at the world's biggest exchange also tighten liquidity before Friday's monthly options expiry on Deribit at 08:00 GMT. --- Earlier: Binance appears hacked, CZ says, as Tether and Circle freeze $1.79B in stablecoins Tether freezes $971M USDT amid suspected Binance hack as crypto sells off --- Binance has stopped part of its withdrawals and stablecoin issuers have locked up $2.4 billion, but the ether that got away keeps this suspected hack on course to be crypto's largest. Summary: Binance temporarily paused withdrawals on multiple networks after more than $3 billion was drained from its Ethereum hot wallets on 29 October. Tether froze more than 1.567 billion USDT and Circle more than 800 million USDC, about $2.4 billion in total. More than $1 billion, mostly ether, remains unfrozen. Binance says user funds are completely safe but hasn't called it a hack or given a loss figure. CZ says it looks like a hack and expects losses to be covered.

title: Nvidia in talks to guarantee Nscale debt tied to $45 billion Anthropic compute deal
body: For Nvidia shares, the trade-off is between locking in demand for its next-generation chips and taking on contingent credit risk tied to a pre-IPO company. That balance may draw closer scrutiny of the off-balance-sheet exposure Nvidia reports in future filings. The report also matters for AI credit more broadly. Guarantees from a highly rated supplier could narrow the spreads that smaller data centre developers pay to borrow, easing one of the funding strains markets have been worried about. Nscale's planned IPO could benefit from the added backing, though investors are likely to ask how much of its revenue depends on financing from its own supplier. --- Tech under pressure, funny this should come out;-) Earnings bloodbath: Intel crashes over 22%, Amazon over 12%. What's coming next? --- Nvidia already sells the chips and owns a stake in the landlord. Now it may co-sign the mortgage too.

title: Morgan Stanley's Wilson sees one final sell-off before US stock correction ends
body: Wilson's roadmap (posted earlier this week) implies near-term downside for semiconductors and AI-linked credit, alongside a buy-the-dip setup for early-cycle sectors once the catalysts clear. That makes AI-linked debt issuance and data centre credit spreads key gauges to watch over the coming weeks. There's also a possible two-stage dollar trade, though this is editorial interpretation rather than Morgan Stanley's view. A final risk-off shock could lift the US dollar on safe-haven demand. If that stress pushes the Fed toward easing, it could also mark a peak in dollar strength. Higher energy prices tied to the Iran conflict remain a risk to the timeline, since they add to the tightening pressure Wilson describes. --- Morgan Stanley thinks the stock correction has one more leg down in it, and that the stress which delivers it may also bring the Fed to the rescue.

title: RBA set for back-to-back hike after hot CPI, says Natixis' Garcia Herrero
body: A back-to-back hike would extend the Australian dollar's rate advantage and keep front-end yields elevated, while any hint that November is the last move could trigger a pullback in both. Fuel is the key transmission channel, so oil prices remain central to the outlook: further crude gains would deepen the pass-through into services and strengthen calls for more tightening. Australian equities, particularly rate-sensitive sectors such as property and consumer discretionary, face added pressure if markets begin to price a longer hiking path. --- Earlier: ING lifts AUD/USD target to 0.71 as it backs a 25bp RBA hike next week --- Fuel is no longer just a petrol-station problem for Australia's inflation, and Natixis expects the RBA to respond again next week.

title: ING lifts AUD/USD target to 0.71 as it backs a 25bp RBA hike next week
body: Front-end Australian yields look most exposed to next week's decision, with roughly 5bp of hike pricing still to close if the RBA moves. A hold would likely hit the Australian dollar hard, given how much of its October strength rests on rate expectations. Oil is a key driver: further gains in crude would add to fuel-led inflation and reinforce the tightening bias, while a sustained pullback could ease pressure on the RBA. The Fed's stance remains the main external constraint on AUD/USD. --- Earlier: RBA set for fifth 2026 hike to 4.85% as banks flag risk of another move in February --- ING likes the Aussie's yield and expects the RBA to add to it next week, but sees the Fed standing between AUD/USD and 0.72. Summary: ING raised its short-term AUD/USD target to 0.71, but doesn't expect a return to 0.72 this quarter It says the Australian dollar offers the best volatility-adjusted short-term carry in G10 ING expects a 25bp RBA hike on 3 November, taking the cash rate to 4.85%, against about 20bp priced Headline CPI hit 4.3% y/y in September, driven almost entirely by fuel-related transport costs Goods and services inflation are both above 4%, and core inflation accelerated A hawkish Fed is expected to keep supporting the US dollar, limiting AUD gains ING has raised its short-term forecast for the Australian dollar to 0.71 against the US dollar, citing the currency's strong October and its attractive yield advantage.

title: ECB to hike once more in December as tighter conditions may not suffice: Deutsche Bank
body: A December "last hike" view mainly affects the euro front end, with Euribor, €STR futures and one- to two-year government bond yields most exposed to shifts in pricing. Capping expectations could reduce volatility further out the curve, while short-dated contracts stay sensitive to each inflation print. Energy is the swing factor: further gains in oil and gas prices would strengthen the case for tightening and could support the euro. Leadership uncertainty adds a policy risk premium into 2027, which could weigh on the single currency if succession becomes politically contested. --- Earlier: investingLive Americas market news wrap: ECB holds, sources report says December hike --- Deutsche Bank thinks the ECB has one more hike in it, and that the coming change of personnel matters less than the price of energy.
